ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46; Civil Code of Quebec, articles 2236 et seq. (societe en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1; Regulation respecting the fees payable to the Registraire des entreprises. For exclusive beneficial-ownership disclosure, Quebec maintains a government-side beneficial owner declaration integrated with the Registraire des entreprises and FINTRAC-required KYC files held by reporting entities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of corporate status / certificate of existence of each foreign corporate partner or general partner, issued not more than 90 days before filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or competent authority of the partner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the home jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention party; otherwise notarization followed by Canadian consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the constitutional/charter documents and register of directors of each foreign corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or notary in the home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized UBO declaration identifying every individual owning or controlling at least 25% of the limited partnership or of any corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary, commissioner for oaths, or equivalent officer in the jurisdiction where the declaration is executed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if executed outside Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for the Quebec registered agent or representative responsible for registration filings and service of process
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each partner or corporate grantor before a notary or commissioner for oaths
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if executed outside Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified identity and address documentary dossier for each UBO, beneficial owner, and signatory (passport, proof of address, professional verification)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary, certified KYC professional, or financial institution in the document's origin jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as required by the receiving authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, UBOs, and authorized signatories against OFAC SDN, United Nations Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, Public Safety Canada/Global Affairs Canada sanctioned persons, and FINTRAC Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) categories. Screening must include domestic and foreign PEPs, heads of state, senior politicians, judges, military officials, shareholders of state-owned enterprises, and close associates. Negative hits trigger enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, senior management approval, and, where required, a suspicious transaction report to FINTRAC. Screening results must be retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Registre des entreprises; online name search and name reservation portal at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, and associated trade-name regulations, the registered name must be in French or must have a French version that appears in the register. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters. A limited partnership must include a legal element such as 'Societe en commandite' or 'S.E.C.'; the name must not falsely suggest corporation status or a regulated activity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying banking, trust, insurance, securities, or lending activity without a license, e.g., 'Bank', 'Trust', 'Insurance', 'Assurance', 'Mutual Fund'
Words implying governmental, municipal, royal, or public authority without authorization, e.g., 'Government', 'Ministry', 'Police', 'Commission', 'Royal', 'University', 'College'
Words implying a regulated profession without the required practising permit, e.g., 'Lawyer', 'Notary', 'Architect', 'Engineer', 'Chartered Accountant'
Words contrary to public order, morality, or obscene expressions under the French-language and public-register rules
Names that are misleadingly identical or confusingly similar to an existing enterprise in the Registraire des entreprises
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the REQ rejects a proposed name, the applicant receives written reasons including the conflicting name or the prohibited token. The applicant may, within 30 days of notification, file a request for administrative review with the REQ using the prescribed review form, attaching corrected French-name alternatives, a coexistence or trademark consent letter if applicable, and evidence of prior use or goodwill. The REQ must acknowledge and decide the review; if the review is denied, the applicant may submit a new name-reservation request or seek judicial review in the Superior Court of Quebec under the Code of Civil Procedure. Name reservations are not automatically renewable; after expiry, a new reservation may be filed if the name remains available.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for a low-risk consulting limited partnership only if it provides a physical street address in Quebec at which legal documents and notices can be received and a natural person or registered agent can accept service. A post-office box or purely digital address does not satisfy the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. For tax and substance purposes, a virtual office alone will not establish commercial substance in Quebec; the partnership should maintain real management oversight, client-facing records, and decision-making evidence in Quebec where possible.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, quantified at approximately 10% annual likelihood for a standard non-licensed market-entry consultancy with clean regulatory status. The risk rises to 25-40% where the entity relies solely on a virtual office, has inconsistent registered data, receives significant cash or high-risk payment rails, or has annual revenue above CAD 1,000,000, because Revenu Quebec and the CRA may conduct unannounced verification visits.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST and federal income tax (My Business Account portal: www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes.html; Business Registration Online: broc-riar.cra-arc.gc.ca); Revenu Québec for Quebec QST and Quebec income tax (clicSÉUR enterprise portal: www.revenuquebec.ca; Registraire des entreprises du Québec for entity registration).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Register the Quebec limited partnership with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ). 2) The general partner applies through Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1 for a CRA Business Number (BN) with a GST/HST account, declaring the legal type as partnership. 3) Register the QST account with Revenu Québec via clicSÉUR using the BN/NEQ (forms LM-1/LM-2) and open the partnership's Québec tax file. 4) Each non-resident limited partner, being deemed to carry on business in Quebec through the LP, obtains its own Canadian identification number for filing T5013/T1044 and Part XIII withholding obligations. 5) File the annual T5013 partnership information return with CRA and the equivalent Quebec partnership return.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. A Canadian limited partnership is fiscally transparent under ITA ss. 96-103 and the mirroring provisions of the Quebec Taxation Act: the partnership computes income at the entity level but is not a taxpayer; each partner's allocable share is taxed in the partner's hands. Non-resident limited partners are deemed to carry on business in Quebec and Canada and are taxable on their Canadian-source business income, subject to treaty protection and Part XIII withholding on allocations and guaranteed payments.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a US-style check-the-box election; partnership classification is statutory, not elective. Available elections: (i) alternative fiscal period election under ITA s. 249.1(4) allowing a non-calendar fiscal year-end for the partnership when all partners are non-calendar-year filers; (ii) s. 103(1) election permitting partners to elect a reasonable allocation of income differing from stated profit-sharing ratios; (iii) designated-member election for T5013 filing purposes; (iv) for GST/HST, the partnership may elect to have the general partner file and remit on behalf of all partners. Hybrid mismatch rules (ITA s. 18.4) apply mechanically where the Quebec LP is treated as opaque by a foreign partner jurisdiction; no election is available, but ex-ante characterization analysis is recommended.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added tax) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax), a semi-autonomous VAT harmonized under the Canada-Quebec Comprehensive Integrated Tax Coordination Agreement.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 - mandatory GST/HST and QST registration is triggered when taxable supplies made in Canada exceed C$30,000 in a single calendar quarter or across four consecutive calendar quarters (small-supplier threshold). Voluntary registration is available below the threshold to claim input tax credits (ITCs) and input tax refunds (IVRs).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping system. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically via GST/HST NETFILE or CRA-approved EDI/API software for registrants above prescribed thresholds. Revenu Québec mandates electronic filing for QST returns and has confirmed a phased introduction of mandatory B2B electronic invoicing and event-based e-reporting beginning in the 2026-2027 period, initially for large enterprises, with XML e-invoices transmitted through certified digital service providers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Advisory and consulting services (ISIC 7020) supplied to a non-resident person are zero-rated under Schedule VI Part V, paragraph 7 of the Excise Tax Act and the mirroring rule in the Quebec Sales Tax Act (Schedule D, services to non-residents), provided: (a) the recipient is not resident in Canada; (b) the service is not performed in connection with real or tangible personal property situated in Canada; and (c) the recipient is not a GST/HST/QST registrant acquiring the service for use in its Canadian commercial activity. The overseas market-entry consultancy scope, which targets foreign markets only, satisfies these criteria if the contract clearly excludes Canadian on-shore deliverables and the benefit is enjoyed outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian export declaration (B13A/CAED or CBSA EDI export reporting) for any tangible incidental deliverables
Bill of lading or airway bill evidencing physical export where applicable
Commercial invoice quoting the zero-rating code (Schedule VI Part V, para. 7) and referencing the non-resident contract
Foreign-currency inward remittance evidence (bank SWIFT or Wise B2B receipt) matched to the invoice
Signed service agreement confirming foreign-market scope and absence of Canadian real/tangible property nexus
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec audit zero-rated consultancy claims against the stated scope-of-work, the non-resident status of the recipient, and actual bank remittance evidence; a finding that services were rendered in or for Canada re-characterizes the supply as taxable at 14.975% (5% GST + 9.975% QST) and permits disallowance of input tax credits. Penalties: GST/HST evasion penalty of up to 200% of the evaded tax (ETA s. 285.1); false statements penalty of the greater of C$250 and 25% of the tax sought (ETA s. 280); gross-negligence penalty of 50% of understated income tax (ITA s. 163.2); Quebec QST evasion penalty of up to C$25,000 plus 125% of evaded QST (Quebec Taxation Act s. 1059); interest runs from the balance-due date. The normal reassessment period is four years but is unlimited where misrepresentation, fraud, or wilful default is established. No statutory Canadian FX repatriation deadline exists; the 180-day benchmark is an administrative intercompany collection and transfer-pricing documentation norm.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BOC) acts as monetary and regulatory authority over retail payment systems; the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) prudentially regulates federally chartered banks; the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administers AML/KYC supervision; there is no standalone foreign-exchange control authority in Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account convertibility and a substantially liberalized capital account. Profits, dividends, interest, royalties, and service fees are freely remittable but are generally subject to Canadian non-resident withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (typically 25%, reduced by treaty) and to FATCA/CRS informational reporting. Capital inflows such as equity or intercompany loans require no routine central bank authorization, but transactions by non-Canadians establishing control of a Canadian business may require notification or review under the Investment Canada Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender mandates or forced conversion timelines for export proceeds. Exporters may maintain receipts in any freely convertible currency in Canadian or foreign bank accounts. Practical compliance requires accurate invoicing, bank deposit records, and tax records under the Income Tax Act and the Excise Tax Act (GST/QST with respect to zero-rated services).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-to-High viability for payment processing only. Offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise can provide cross-border payment and multi-currency facilitation without being chartered banks in Canada, but they may not take deposits or offer lending products. They must register as a money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC, and if operating in Quebec, likely coordinate with the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) with respect to money-services business licensing. Payments under the ISIC 7020 advisory scope can use EMI rails for low-value disbursements, but capital escrow and high-value treaty-sensitive flows should remain in tier-1 Canadian banking channels.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No explicit statutory requirement mandates that all directors appear physically in Canada for account opening, but Canadian banks generally require robust identity verification for non-resident entity accounts. Remote onboarding is available when corporate documents are notarized, legalized or apostilled, and when certified true copies of passport, articles, partnership agreement, and register of directors are supplied. Most tier-1 institutions will require a video interview or a Canadian resident authorized signatory with a physical mailing address. For a Quebec limited partnership, the general partner must be registered in the Quebec enterprise registrar (Registraire des entreprises) and a bilingual or notarized excerpt may be mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident structure with no substantive Canadian tax presence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current business plan, Canadian revenue agency account registration, registered office address in Quebec, audited or unaudited financial statements, beneficial ownership diagram, source of funds and wealth documentation, professional legal opinion confirming no passive shell character.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited partnership with opaque beneficial ownership layers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full limited partnership agreement, certificate of formation, Quebec enterprise registrar excerpt, register of limited and general partners identifying all 25% or greater beneficial owners, plus a sworn declaration of the general partner and each significant owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Overseas market entry consultancy with fees routed through multiple jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed service contract with defined deliverables, itemized invoices, client-specific work product evidence, comprehensive cross-border transaction flow map, counterparty KYC questionnaires, and tax residence certificates for all beneficiaries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No physical office and reliance on virtual workspace
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Virtual office service agreement, lease for any operational closet office in Quebec, director and employee credentials, professional licensing, client references, and video-recorded site inspection of the virtual office's local address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment flow involving high-risk or sanctioned-adjacent jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screened counterparty sanctions letters, transaction-level risk assessment, delivery of advisory milestones, client anti-money-laundering due diligence files, duplicate invoice documentation, and an explicit undertaking not to facilitate restricted goods or services.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward capital for the Quebec limited partnership should be routed via SWIFT MT103 with an instructive statement referencing the partnership's Quebec enterprise registry number (NEQ), Canadian Business Number (BN), and transaction purpose. Equity contributions require no prior foreign-exchange approval; however, intercompany loan advances must be documented with a formal loan agreement, interest rate benchmark, and repayment schedule to satisfy Canadian tax thin capitalization and transfer-pricing rules. Investment Canada Act notification is mandatory for any acquisition of control that crosses statutory thresholds. Wires should designate a purpose code consistent with the OECD ISO 20022 categorization, such as direct investment or intercompany lending, and the receiving bank should receive an executed source-of-funds declaration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound advisory fee settlements should use SWIFT MT103 (International Wire) or Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP600) when bank intermediation is required. For payments to overseas consultants, payment instructions should include complete invoice numbers, service descriptions, and tax treaty documentation to support reduced withholding rates where applicable. Same-day funding within Canada occurs via Payments Canada's Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or the new Real-Time Rail (RTR); cross-border clearing in USD can be effected through CHIPS/Fedwire correspondent accounts, while EUR or Asian settlements require attention to time-zone cut-offs and intermediary bank charges. For low-value recurring consulting payments, an MSB rail such as Wise B2B may be used, but high-dollar capital escrow disbursements should be kept in tier-1 banking channels with audit-grade documentary trails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright foreign exchange forward contracts with a Canadian or foreign Schedule-I bank
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies without active deliverable markets, provided the underlying exposure is genuine trade or investment risk
Plain-vanilla foreign currency swaps and cross-currency swaps
FX options (European-style) for hedging budget-rate uncertainty on cross-border consulting receipts and disbursements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) of the limited partnership with updated general partner and establishment information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: the declaration window opens on the first day of the third month before the registration anniversary and closes on the anniversary date; a tardive filing is accepted only with an additional administrative tariff.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late annual declaration attracts an additional REQ tariff and blocks issuance of attestation documents; knowingly false declarations attract monetary penalties of CA$500–CA$5,000. After two consecutive years of non-filing, REQ serves a notice of default and may administratively strike off (radier) the LP 60 days after the notice, extinguishing the LP's capacity to operate a registrable commercial activity in Québec.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Partnership Information Return (T5013) and partner T5013 slips and summary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year partnerships file by March 31 of the year following the fiscal period end; non-calendar-year partnerships file no later than the later of March 31 and six months after fiscal period end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Income Tax Act subsection 162(4) penalty of CA$10 per day for the return and CA$10 per day for each omitted partner slip, minimum CA$100 and maximum CA$2,500 per return; wilful omissions may also attract gross-negligence penalties and partner filing restrictions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Québec Partnership Information Return (CO-17) and RL-15/RL-16 information slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the federal T5013: on or before March 31 following fiscal period end for calendar-year partnerships, or no later than the later of March 31 and six months after fiscal period end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file attracts Taxation Act (Québec) late-reporting penalties of CA$10 per day, minimum CA$100 and maximum CA$2,500; repeated omission allows Revenu Québec to cease recognizing the allocation of partnership income claimed by partners.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on Québec limited partnerships by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. An independent audit becomes compulsory when the partnership agreement or a lender covenant requires it, or when the partnership meets CRA large-partnership information-reporting thresholds (generally 500 or more partners, or C$50 million or more in gross assets or annual revenue), obliging the preparation of T5013 Schedule 50 with certified accountant involvement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook – Accounting, Part II) is the applicable Canadian local GAAP for private limited partnerships; IFRS (Part I) applies if the partnership becomes a publicly accountable enterprise or the partnership agreement mandates IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each annual REQ declaration must confirm the identity of all general partners (commandités) and, where a general partner is a legal person, disclose that entity's directors and ultimate controlling owners. Transfers of limited-partner interests are not public UBO filings at REQ; they are recorded internally in the register of partners, reported in the annual T5013/CO-17 allocation schedules, and reflected in the next annual declaration only if the general-partner structure changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (limited and general partners, capital accounts, and profit/loss allocation percentages)
General Partner Minute Book (partnership decisions, consents, capital call resolutions, and annual financial statement approvals)
Register of Ultimate Controlling Owners (maintained where the general partner is a legal person)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$300–US$900 per annum for a Québec commercial registered office, service-of-process agent, and corporate secretarial domiciliation service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$4,000–US$15,000 per engagement for a full statutory-style audit of a small consulting LP; US$1,800–US$4,000 for a review engagement where external assurance is only contractually required
